subject: Og-woi People's Orchard and Garden
comment: Dear Salt Lake City Council Members, My name is Deanna Taylor and I live in the Fairpark Community of Salt Lake City. Thank you for the opportunity to offer my public comment. I am writing to you about the Og-woi People's Orchard and Garden, for which I am a volunteer and live nearby. I am writing in particular to highlight the enormous support our communities have put forward over the past month. Over 300 people have signed the petition to Save the Og-woi. I direct your attention to this webpage, "What People are Saying About the Og-woi". I would like to highlight here some of those comments, all from the zip code 84116, the area of the Og-woi, and represents just a fraction of the over 100 comments in the petition: This project is a stellar example of actual Community Driven Community Stewardship of the Public Lands, using only Community resources so far. It also closely aligns with several other initiatives that the City is managing Grant money for, particularly the Love Your Block Grant and the Food and Equity Gardens Grant programs. The garden is a great addition to the neighborhood and the fairpark area. Many people love working in the garden and enjoying all it has to offer. It's also refreshing to have something beautiful on a piece of land that wasn't previously used for anything other than growing weeds and being an eye sore. I can think of no reason the Og-woi People's Orchard should be removed - only reasons as to why it should stay. This is such an important community resource and something SLC should be doing more of, not less! This beautiful garden brings so much life and sustenance to this community, our neighborhood, and the Jordan River Trail. The Og-Woi garden is a beautiful space that has taught me so much about gardening and community. The city would be doing itself a disservice to take it away from its constituents. I've been going there since before my son was born and I plan on raising him there to value community and gardening The Og-woi is an example of how food can be accessible to our community. It has proven to be a space that contributes to the overall health of the environment and to learn and teach community resiliency. Numerous families and individuals have benefited from the joys of the Og-woi People's Orchard and Garden, once a neglected space filled with puncture vine - transformed into a space of beauty and sustenance.This garden is exactly the sort of project I want to see in my community. It: 1. revitalizes unused space 2. brings different people together 3. enhances our community resilience 4. improves access to food and 5. honors people who were here before us and those who work to make things better now. The city should be overjoyed that this happened organically and failing over themselves to support it, not trying to stop it. Mental health space to grieve a loved one, a healthy space to learn more about nature, a space to garden, a space to give back to the community, a space of learning, a public space, a space to find peace at times, a space of a home, and a community space to come back to educate others. A visiting space for social events, a space of contribution, a family space, a community leader space, and a space that shouldn't be having a dispute over. Let us know how we can help. It would be a shame to lose another community garden in the valley. I believe that this garden is a benefit to everyone around it. With little to no risk of it being there my belief is that everyone should be able to reap the benefits and beauty of having this amazing area in our city I have worked at the Cannon Health Building since 2013, and have owned my home in this neighborhood since 2020. The Og-Woi garden is beautiful and exemplifies care for the Earth, the river, and the community. It's important to me that it be allowed to continue. Beautifies and utilizes an otherwise unused space. I applaud what the goal is with this project and the benefits to people, especially for those on the west side. I love walking past the garden with my dogs daily. It brings me a sense of connection to my community. It is an invaluable resource and we should be expanding community gardens, not reducing them. This garden is a beautiful and important piece of our community. It helps bring people together from all over the neighborhood, and is a welcome sight for visitors or prospective home buyers (it certainly was for me before we moved in). It deserves to be not only protected, but expanded upon for the good of all of us in Rose Park. It represents the values that make Utah such a great state to live in. I love the mission, and the development that this project brings to both the neighborhood and the Jordan River, which is so often in need of improvement. It's important to support people and projects with this much of a sense of passion, care, and civic engagement. I am asking that you support the Og-woi People's Orchard and Garden, a true community asset. Thank you, Deanna Taylor

subject: Og-woi garden
comment: Folks, I think removing Og-woi is bad idea. It's a community garden. They did the research on environmental contaminants, and followed the recommendations. Tom has been tested for lead contamination and none is found. There isn't a relevant health reason to remove it. I know a neighbor keeps complaining, but I honestly can't see how it harms the neighbors. This feels like a PR debacle. I genuinely think it's a beloved community garden, and if you require them to post notices or make it more accessible, they'll be happy to do so. Please consider the human factor - community gardens are exactly what we want folks to be doing right now. Getting out of the house. Interacting. Building friendships. This is good community at work. Please keep the Og-Woi. - Wendy

subject: Concerned about loose dogs in Sugarhouse
comment: Dear Councilwoman Fowler, I am writing as a member of your district who moved to this neighborhood almost a year ago from South Salt Lake. I will preface these comments by saying that I enjoy this neighborhood and appreciate the efforts of our city council that make Salt Lake City a great place to live. My concern is with off-leash dogs, something I virtually never experienced in South Salt Lake or Liberty Wells despite taking my own two dogs for runs and walks in those neighborhoods every day for the several years I lived there. By contrast, I have observed a significant number of loose dogs in my new neighborhood, and unfortunately, a lot of those dogs are not well-trained and cannot be trusted to stay within the boundaries of their owners' properties. I have neighbors whose multiple dogs are never leashed and frequently run up the street out of control or intrude into my yard, despite my attempts to communicate with them that this is a problem. I have neighbors whose dogs have chased my dogs from 30+ feet away. Just in the past week, my two dogs have been approached -- and not always politely -- by at least five dogs, the majority of which left their own properties to pursue us. My dogs, while leashed, have even been attacked by an off-leash dog in Sugarhouse Park, an incidence which I reported to SLCo Animal Control, who were seemingly powerless to do anything about the attack -- even to simply enforce the leash laws, which would have ensured that such a dog attack was far less likely. Like most dogs, my dogs do not appreciate being approached by unfamiliar off-leash dogs. I have employed extensive training to help my dogs handle this stress, but ultimately, there are leash laws in the city, and those laws should be enforced. It is my right to enjoy our public spaces without the constant fear that a neighbor's unleashed dog will run into my dogs' space and potentially cause a fight. I understand that budgets are limited and that resources can only be stretched so far, but is there anything that can be done? It seems to me that it would only take an Animal Control officer taking a leashed dog for a few Saturday afternoon walks to encounter plenty of people to ticket and educate. Sincerely, Nancy Radigan-Hoffman

subject: increased sewer charges?
comment: Hi, we received a letter informing us of increased sewage consumption this past winter and we will begin seeing an increase of our sewage charges up to $67.90 per month? This is nearly double what we have been paying for sewage on our water bill to date. As of March 16 - we did have a sewage backup, and it was fixed that day. Since then, the sewage usage would be at least 50% less than what it typically is because of the pending repairs, therefore, we would like to know why we're being told our consumption has increased and we're being penalized for it. If we need to provide documentation of the repairs, please let us know what information you need. Sincerely, Ben & Amanda Pendleton

subject: Pedestrian safety
comment: Dear SLC council, We really have an out of control situation regarding pedestrian safety with speeding drivers. I used the WALK button to "safely" cross 2100 south in SugarHouse at McClelland street. The light turned red, and one car stopped appropriately so I could cross...however a speeding SUV nearly ran me over as I got a quarter of the way across. It must've been going about 40 MPH...maybe more. He never slowed. Ran right thru the red light, literally inches in front of me. I've also been nearly run over as a pedestrian here on 1900 east near Clayton middle school. The limit is now 20 MPH, but the norm is 30 to 40. I try to drive the posted speed limit on 1900 east, and a truck didn't want to be behind me, so he passed me...by going into the OPPOSING LANE. I have several more examples...including video of my step mom who has Parkinson's disease trying to cross 1900 east at a corner using her cane...but cars won't stop! We need speed bumps...motorcycle officer speed traps...and speed trap CAMERAS on 1900 East. Pedestrian safety...driver behavior...is much worse here than in Los Angeles...or even Delhi, India! Isn't an ounce of prevention worth a pound of cure? Sincerely, Jeff Myers

subject: Sunnyside Baseball Stadium - Stop it!
comment: Dear City Council Members, I am a resident of the Harvard, Yale district - one of the city's most beautiful neighborhoods. I was shocked that the University of Utah plans to build a large baseball facility on our Sunnyside Community Park!! Do not allow this to happen. Our community is already overrun and filled with garbage during every Utes football game. Our neighborhood parking is completely taken over. This new baseball stadium cannot be added to that mess. Moreover, every day/evening/weekend those fields are full of local residents playing soccer, flag football, baseball, and throwing the balls for their dogs. Where is all this supposed to happen when that Baseball field gets built? We have a very nice Baseball facility on 1300 S. Smith's Ball Field, that is perfect for the University's team to continue playing. I am also concerned because there was no community input or discussion. Please do not let this happen!! It will affect the livability of my neighborhood, the value of my house, and bring more crime, garbage, traffic issues into one of the city's best neighborhoods Thank you for fighting for us. Chris Christopher Gregg PhD. Associate Professor of Neurobiology and Human Genetics

subject: Proposed Baseball Facility on Sunnyside
comment: Good Afternoon, I am a resident of the Harvard, Yale district. I was just informed that the University of Utah plans to build a large baseball facility on our Sunnyside Community Park!! I am shocked that there hasn't been any community discussion or input on this project. Sunnyside park is used everyday by teams and local residents playing soccer, flag football, baseball, and throwing the balls for their dogs. Plus, parking is already insane when we have Utes games and can't imagine what it will be like if you add in another massive venue. In addition, there isn't the road infrastructure to accommodate the increased traffic, which will result in a massive amount of traffic flying through the community to try to avoid traffic congestion. What are the plans in place to prevent this? There is a perfectly good Baseball facility on 1300 S, Smith's Ball Field. Why are there plans to build another one? Please let me know if there is anything I can do to help prevent this from happening. Denise Gregg
